title: The Tower is Going Home
statementMd:
On a chessboard with a width of $10^9$ and a height of $10^9$, the rows are numbered from bottom to top from $1$ to $10^9$, and the columns are numbered from left to right from $1$ to $10^9$. Therefore, for each cell of the chessboard you can assign the coordinates $(x,y)$, where $x$ is the column number and $y$ is the row number.

Every day there are fights between black and white pieces on this board. Today, the black ones won, but at what price? Only the rook survived, and it was driven into the lower left corner — a cell with coordinates $(1,1)$. But it is still happy, because the victory has been won and it's time to celebrate it! In order to do this, the rook needs to go home, namely — on the **upper side** of the field (that is, in any cell that is in the row with number $10^9$).

Everything would have been fine, but the treacherous white figures put spells on some places of the field before the end of the game. There are two types of spells:

- Vertical. Each of these is defined by one number $x$. Such spells create an infinite *blocking line* between the columns $x$ and $x+1$.
- Horizontal. Each of these is defined by three numbers $x_1$, $x_2$, $y$. Such spells create a *blocking segment* that passes through the top side of the cells, which are in the row $y$ and in columns from $x_1$ to $x_2$ inclusive. The peculiarity of these spells is that it is **impossible** for a certain pair of such spells to have a common point. Note that horizontal spells can have common points with vertical spells.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/90c70dd895c54815d19d5dc78635ba32c56114b6.png)

An example of a chessboard.

Let's recall that the rook is a chess piece that in one move can move to any point that is in the same row or column with its initial position. In our task, the rook can move from the cell $(r_0,c_0)$ into the cell $(r_1,c_1)$ only under the condition that $r_1 = r_0$ or $c_1 = c_0$ and there is no *blocking lines* or *blocking segments* between these cells (For better understanding, look at the samples).

Fortunately, the rook can remove spells, but for this it has to put tremendous efforts, therefore, it wants to remove the minimum possible number of spells in such way, that after this it can return home. Find this number!

## Input

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $m$ ($0 \le n,m \le 10^5$) — the number of vertical and horizontal spells.

Each of the following $n$ lines contains one integer $x$ ($1 \le x \lt 10^9$) — the description of the vertical spell. It will create a *blocking line* between the columns of $x$ and $x+1$.

Each of the following $m$ lines contains three integers $x_1$, $x_2$ and $y$ ($1 \le x_{1} \le x_{2} \le 10^9$, $1 \le y \lt 10^9$) — the numbers that describe the horizontal spell. It will create a *blocking segment* that passes through the top sides of the cells that are in the row with the number $y$, in columns from $x_1$ to $x_2$ inclusive.

It is guaranteed that all spells are different, as well as the fact that for each pair of horizontal spells it is true that the segments that describe them do not have common points.

## Output

In a single line print one integer — the minimum number of spells the rook needs to remove so it can get from the cell $(1,1)$ to at least one cell in the row with the number $10^9$

## Note

In the first sample, in order for the rook return home, it is enough to remove the second horizontal spell.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/79ba3e377dac6034a170469f1b79bf64978aede3.png) Illustration for the first sample. On the left it shows how the field looked at the beginning. On the right it shows how the field looked after the deletion of the second horizontal spell. It also shows the path, on which the rook would be going home.

In the second sample, in order for the rook to return home, it is enough to remove the only vertical spell. If we tried to remove just one of the horizontal spells, it would not allow the rook to get home, because it would be blocked from above by one of the remaining horizontal spells (either first one or second one), and to the right it would be blocked by a vertical spell.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7605a14fd36ffc8483622bcccb2053ffac4693c3.png) Illustration for the second sample. On the left it shows how the field looked at the beginning. On the right it shows how it looked after the deletion of the vertical spell. It also shows the path, on which the rook would be going home.

In the third sample, we have two horizontal spells that go through the whole field. These spells can not be bypassed, so we need to remove both of them.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8722835dc84cd3988660017beacd92a58254528f.png) Illustration for the third sample. On the left it shows how the field looked at the beginning. On the right it shows how the field looked after the deletion of the horizontal spells. It also shows the path, on which the rook would be going home.

In the fourth sample, we have no spells, which means that we do not need to remove anything.

In the fifth example, we can remove the first vertical and third horizontal spells.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6ff2f6d42f11a3f3dcea6f4f2fc7d1cc20557a06.png) Illustration for the fifth sample. On the left it shows how the field looked at the beginning. On the right it shows how it looked after the deletions. It also shows the path, on which the rook would be going home.
statementZhMd:
在一个宽度为 $10^9$、高度为 $10^9$ 的棋盘上，行从下到上编号为 $1$ 到 $10^9$，列从左到右编号为 $1$ 到 $10^9$。因此，对于棋盘上的每个格子，都可以用坐标 $(x,y)$ 表示，其中 $x$ 是列号，$y$ 是行号。

每天，黑白双方的棋子都会在棋盘上进行战斗。今天黑方获胜了，但代价是什么呢？只有车存活了下来，并且被逼到了左下角——坐标为 $(1,1)$ 的格子。但它仍然很高兴，因为胜利已经到手，是时候庆祝了！为了庆祝，车需要回到家，也就是到达棋盘的**上边界**（即行号为 $10^9$ 的任意格子）。

一切本来都很顺利，但狡猾的白方棋子在战斗结束前对棋盘上的一些位置施加了魔法。魔法有两种类型：

- 垂直魔法。每个垂直魔法由一个数 $x$ 定义。它会在第 $x$ 列和第 $x+1$ 列之间生成一条无限长的*阻挡线*。
- 水平魔法。每个水平魔法由三个数 $x_1$、$x_2$、$y$ 定义。它会生成一条*阻挡线段*，该线段经过第 $y$ 行、列号从 $x_1$ 到 $x_2$（包含两端）的格子的上边界。这类魔法有一个特点：任意两个这样的魔法对应的线段都不可能有公共点。注意，水平魔法对应的线段可以与垂直魔法对应的阻挡线有公共点。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/90c70dd895c54815d19d5dc78635ba32c56114b6.png)

棋盘示例。

我们来回忆一下，车是一种棋子，它可以在一步内移动到与初始位置处于同一行或同一列的任意点。在本题中，车只能从格子 $(r_0,c_0)$ 移动到格子 $(r_1,c_1)$，且必须满足 $r_1 = r_0$ 或 $c_1 = c_0$，并且这两个格子之间不存在*阻挡线*或*阻挡线段*（为了更好地理解，请参见样例）。

幸运的是，车可以移除魔法，但这需要付出巨大的努力。因此，它希望移除尽可能少的魔法，使自己能够回到家。请求出这个最少数量！

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $n$ 和 $m$（$0 \le n,m \le 10^5$）——垂直魔法和水平魔法的数量。

接下来的 $n$ 行，每行包含一个整数 $x$（$1 \le x \lt 10^9$）——垂直魔法的描述。它会在第 $x$ 列和第 $x+1$ 列之间生成一条*阻挡线*。

接下来的 $m$ 行，每行包含三个整数 $x_1$、$x_2$ 和 $y$（$1 \le x_{1} \le x_{2} \le 10^9$，$1 \le y \lt 10^9$）——描述水平魔法的数值。它会生成一条*阻挡线段*，该线段经过第 $y$ 行、列号从 $x_1$ 到 $x_2$（包含两端）的格子的上边界。

保证所有魔法各不相同，并且对于每一对水平魔法，它们对应的线段都没有公共点。

## 输出格式

在一行中输出一个整数——车需要移除的最少魔法数量，使其能够从格子 $(1,1)$ 到达行号为 $10^9$ 的至少一个格子。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，为了让车回到家，只需移除第二个水平魔法。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/79ba3e377dac6034a170469f1b79bf64978aede3.png) 第一个样例的示意图。左图展示了棋盘最初的样子，右图展示了移除第二个水平魔法后的样子。同时还展示了车回家时所经过的路径。

在第二个样例中，为了让车回到家，只需移除唯一的垂直魔法。如果只尝试移除其中一个水平魔法，车仍然无法回到家，因为剩下的另一个水平魔法会从上方阻挡它（第一个或第二个水平魔法），而右侧又会被垂直魔法阻挡。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7605a14fd36ffc8483622bcccb2053ffac4693c3.png) 第二个样例的示意图。左图展示了棋盘最初的样子，右图展示了移除垂直魔法后的样子。同时还展示了车回家时所经过的路径。

在第三个样例中，有两个贯穿整个棋盘的水平魔法。这些魔法无法绕过，因此我们需要移除它们两个。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8722835dc84cd3988660017beacd92a58254528f.png) 第三个样例的示意图。左图展示了棋盘最初的样子，右图展示了移除水平魔法后的样子。同时还展示了车回家时所经过的路径。

在第四个样例中，没有任何魔法，这意味着我们不需要移除任何东西。

在第五个样例中，我们可以移除第一个垂直魔法和第三个水平魔法。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6ff2f6d42f11a3f3dcea6f4f2fc7d1cc20557a06.png) 第五个样例的示意图。左图展示了棋盘最初的样子，右图展示了移除魔法后的样子。同时还展示了车回家时所经过的路径。
